featured_promo.title: 12 Bills, 2 Programs. Here's What's at Stake for California Real Estate.
featured_promo.body: A few of us spent yesterday in Sacramento at C.A.R. Legislative Day. We came back with the full scorecard on the bills that will shape how you write contracts, list properties, and have the affordability conversation with clients this year. From condo deposit caps (AB 1406) to rent control changes (AB 1157) to a CAR-sponsored HOA reform (SB 1238). The breakdown is now live on the Agent Hub.
featured_promo.quote: Only 1 in 6 California households can afford a median-priced home. That's the reason every bill on this page matters.

economy.commentary:
The Fed held rates steady for the third time this year, exactly as the market expected. The 10-year jumped 8bp to 4.42% as the bond market repriced the "no near-term cuts" reality. That's the source of today's mortgage tick to 6.50%.

WTI pulled back -2.4% to $104.35, but Brent ripped to $119.75 (+6% intraday) after Trump told Axios the U.S. Blockade of Iran stays until Tehran signs a nuclear deal. The WTI/Brent spread is now historically wide, domestic oil cooling while seaborne supply gets squeezed.

Gold ticked back up to $4,575 as the rate-hold + Iran combo kept safe-haven flows live.

The U.S. Treasury froze $344M in USDT tied to Iran's Revolutionary Guard, the largest crypto seizure of this conflict, cutting off a primary money-movement channel Iran has used for decades. Stablecoin censorship at a new scale.

Meanwhile, Robinhood (HOOD -13.24%) cratered as crypto revenue fell 47% YoY. The retail trader has left the building. Galaxy's pivot to AI hosting yesterday and now this. The crypto-firm earnings model is being rewritten in real time.

real_estate.homebuilder: Fed Holds, Rates Tick to 6.50%; Spring Rebound Stalls Second Year Running
real_estate.commentary:
The Fed delivered exactly what the bond market priced in: no cut, third pause this year. Kevin Warsh cleared the Senate Banking Committee for the chair seat; Powell announced he's staying on as a Fed Governor after his term ends May 15. Stability at the top, but no relief for buyers. Mortgage rates ticked up to 6.50%, and the 10-year jumped to 4.42% as the bond market reprices the "no cuts soon" reality. The bigger structural read: America's spring housing rebound is stalling for the second year in a row. The mechanics are familiar. Homeowners locked into 3% rates aren't moving, buyers are waiting for prices to drop, and inventory is piling up. And yet, purchase applications are up 21% YoY, driven by high-income buyers who are tuning out the Iran/oil headlines and just transacting. That's the listing-agent opening: the buyer at the door right now is committed and qualified.
🏛️ FROM SACRAMENTO TO YOUR CLOSING TABLE
Here's What We Brought Back From C.A.R. Legislative Day.
Here's what every agent on the team should know. AB 1406 would double the condo deposit forfeiture cap to 6%; at our local $670K median condo price, that's a buyer forfeiting up to $40,200. AB 1157 would tighten rent caps and remove the SFH exemption that protects natural-person owners. SB 1238 (CAR-sponsored) brings overdue HOA transparency and condo financing reform.
Every one of these is the macro version of a closing conversation you're already having.
